lines.speaker: safehouse_keeper
lines.text: Green pennant. You know what it means or you'd not have come up the alley, and if you don't: cellar's dry, there's a pot on, and nobody here asks names or sides.

lines.speaker: safehouse_keeper
lines.text: Four generations. My great-great-grandmother wouldn't sell this corner in 2031 — turned down money when they had none — and every one of us since has been stuck with what that turned into, which is this, which is a door that opens at night.

lines.speaker: safehouse_keeper
lines.text: You're looking at that sign like you've seen it before. It's older than the water. Older than most of what's left standing on this coast.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It is the same board. Scorched along one edge, green pennant on the left, and you were standing underneath it a hundred and seventeen years ago this morning.
